author: worker-2
text:
The supplied vulnerable program reads at most 64 bytes into a 64-byte buffer, so `n` can never exceed 64. Its abort condition `n > 88` is therefore unreachable for any input file. The patched program only prints the byte count, so any candidate file will make both programs exit cleanly; no file can trigger a nonzero exit in the vulnerable version.

I would still test with files of lengths 0, 64, and larger (e.g., 1 KB) to confirm `fread` behavior, and inspect `submit.sh` to see whether the grader compiles the sources or uses prebuilt binaries. I would also check whether the intended vulnerability was a different check or buffer size; as written, the crash condition is logically impossible.
